sections.html: Evans is the smallest county in this part of Georgia, with 11,028 residents as of July 2025 and 183 square miles of coastal plain. Claxton holds the courthouse and the most people. Growth since 2020 is 2.3 percent. Owned homes are worth $138,200 at the median, rent is $719, and owners occupy about two of every three homes. The county issued just 25 building permits in 2025, so resales dominate the market. Local businesses are exempt from tax on certain inventory classes, which matches the freeport exemption the assessors describe.

sections.h2: Where the Evans County tax offices are
sections.html:
The commissioner's counter is in Claxton, and the assessor answers on the same county line.

  • Tax Commissioner: Suite 4 at 201 Freeman Street in Claxton, or by mail at P.O. Box 685; call 912-739-1147 between 8:15 and 4:30 on weekdays.
  • Main county line: 912-739-1141, where option 1 reaches both tax offices. Expect a lunch closing from noon to 1.
  • Records: parcel and exemption information appears on the assessor's qPublic pages.

With a small staff, the office would rather receive faxed or emailed paperwork and send answers back, though visitors may still look through records at the counter. Start a payoff request early, because the phones stay busy around the deadline.

sections.h2: What Evans County charges when taxes are late
sections.html:
The late-fee schedule is short. The deadline is December 20. Every month after it adds 1 percent in interest, and a flat 10 percent penalty arrives with day 91.

Evans County due date, late charges and lien
StepWhat happens
Due dateDecember 20 each year
Interest1 percent added every month after the due date
PenaltyOne-time 10 percent after 90 days
Lien (fi. fa.)Filed on the Execution Docket with the court clerk once taxes are past due

A fi. fa. can follow your credit for as long as seven years. The bill is addressed to the owner, since the commissioner cannot tell who holds the mortgage or whether an escrow account pays the tax. Mortgage companies ask for the figures every year, so make sure yours has them.

Values come from the Board of Tax Assessors. A changed value comes with a notice, and you have 45 days from that notice to object. If the board holds firm, the file moves on its own to the County Board of Equalization, which schedules a hearing. An arbitrator can stand in for that hearing, and superior court sits above both. Only three arguments are accepted:

  • Whether the property is taxable at all.
  • The value placed on it.
  • Whether that value is uniform with similar properties.

Grumbling about the size of the bill does not count, since the bill flows from the millage rate. Mail the appeal early so the postmark lands inside the window. Taxable value is 40 percent of market value.

Homestead applications are handled at the commissioner's office between January 1 and April 1, and an approved exemption carries forward each year. Ownership and residence on January 1 are required. File again if the deed changes hands, if a name is corrected on the deed, or if you move up to another type.

The assessor's page describes a standard $2,000 reduction, a $4,000 reduction for those 65 and up who pass an income test, a school-tax reduction of up to $10,000 starting at age 62, and $50,000 for qualifying disabled veterans and certain surviving spouses. Ask the assessors for the current income limits. A deferral program also exists for low-income seniors, and the deferred amount is due when the home changes owners.

Farmland and timber follow separate rules. A Conservation Use filing must reach the assessors by April 1 with a $10 fee, and it commits the land to a qualifying use for ten years. Breaking the covenant can cost double the taxes saved. The deadline for freeport inventory filings is the same April 1.

sections.h2: Before you close on an Evans County sale
sections.html:
Get the commissioner's payoff on paper before the closing table. Older years are cleared first, and the sale contract settles who bears the current bill.

  • Clear any fi. fa. before the title search turns it up.
  • Once the deed is recorded, give the commissioner the buyer's mailing address.
  • With an escrow account, notify your lender after payoff.
  • Hold on to your warranty deed copy; the court clerk can supply recorded ones.

Acreage adds one more step. A buyer who keeps the original use of Conservation Use land can sign the covenant and avoid a penalty, but a change of use inside the ten years triggers all of them.

sections.h2: Why a seller might choose a cash buyer
sections.html: Someone paying cash and accepting the house as is does not argue over repairs, which helps when a tax bill or lien already sits on the parcel. There is no lender appraisal to wait on, and a fi. fa. can be paid from proceeds at closing. Speed and condition drive the choice. Either way, the commissioner's payoff comes first, so request it as soon as you decide to sell and give your closing agent the figure.

sections.h2: What to ask the offices before listing
sections.html: Two short calls cover most of what a seller needs. Ask the commissioner for the balance on every year, whether any fi. fa. is recorded, and the current payoff good through your target closing date. Ask the assessors whether your homestead is active, whether any acreage sits in a covenant, and when the next notice is expected. Write down names and dates. Phones stay busy near December 20, so calling in the spring is easier than calling in the week before a closing.

faqs.q: When does Evans County expect payment of the annual bill?
faqs.a: The date is December 20. Interest of 1 percent accrues monthly afterward, and the one-time 10 percent penalty comes after 90 days.

faqs.q: Does the Evans County Tax Commissioner mail my bill to the lender?
faqs.a: No. It goes to the owner, since the office has no record of lienholders or escrow arrangements. Lenders ask the office for amounts each year.

faqs.q: What is the window to contest an Evans County value?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the notice date. File with the Board of Tax Assessors, and an unchanged case moves to the Board of Equalization unless you elect arbitration.

faqs.q: What does a fi. fa. mean on an Evans County parcel?
faqs.a: It is a lien the commissioner records with the court clerk when taxes run past due. It can weigh on your credit for up to seven years, so settle it before selling.

faqs.q: Where do Evans County homeowners file for homestead?
faqs.a: At the commissioner's office in Claxton, from January 1 to April 1. Dial 912-739-1141 and press option 1 for questions. An approved exemption renews itself until ownership changes.
